name: ZDeceptron
comment: DELIBERATELY MINIMAL. This grammar classifies tokens only — keywords, literals, comments, and type names. It does NOT attempt to model structure, scope, or the several roles of `is`, because a regular expression cannot distinguish them and a grammar that tries will disagree with the real parser. Structural and semantic highlighting is the job of the language server, which asks the compiler instead of guessing.

patterns.comment: The block literal is listed first because `"""` also starts with the one-line rule's quote, and the one-line rule would take only the first two characters of it. The lexer resolves the same ambiguity the same way, by longest match.
patterns.name: string.quoted.triple.zdeceptron

patterns.comment: `state`, optionally preceded by `secret` and `trusted` in that order, followed by the name being declared.
A component is used exactly where a built-in element is, so its name is highlighted as a tag rather than as a function.
A route declares the site's URLs, and its name is a type exactly as a `choice`'s is.

A claim and its evidence: `test "…"` with an indented `expect`. Both words are soft keywords in the lexer, so they are highlighted only where the grammar admits them — after `test` comes quoted text, and `expect` opens the line under it.
The placements are the core of the language and are highlighted distinctly.
patterns.name: storage.modifier.placement.zdeceptron

patterns.comment: `unique` marks the record field that is a row's identity. A modifier rather than a control word, so it reads like `secret` and `trusted` do.
patterns.name: storage.modifier.unique.zdeceptron
support.type.builtin.zdeceptron
patterns.comment: `Handle` is a base type name like `Text`, not a constructor: a program writes it on a `foreign`'s `takes` and `gives` lines and nowhere else. `new` is deliberately absent from this file, as `foreign`, `takes`, `gives`, `pure`, `every`, `after` and `frame` are: they are soft keywords, so they are ordinary identifiers everywhere outside one clause and highlighting them would colour a parameter named `new`, or a field named `frame`, as a keyword.
Capitalised identifiers are user types or view elements. Distinguishing the two needs the compiler, so both share a scope here.
patterns.name: entity.name.type.zdeceptron

patterns.comment: `is` does three jobs: declaration, named argument, and equality. A regular expression cannot distinguish them, so all three share one scope. The language server assigns accurate scopes via semantic tokens.
patterns.name: keyword.other.is.zdeceptron
